entries.name: Back-end development
entries.definition: Building and maintaining the server-side parts of software, such as application logic, databases and APIs.

entries.name: Backbone.js
entries.definition: A lightweight JavaScript library that gives web applications structure through models, views, collections and routers.

entries.name: BACnet
entries.definition: A communication protocol for building automation and control systems, standardised as ASHRAE 135 and ISO 16484-5.

entries.name: Bacon.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript library for functional reactive programming that models events and changing values as observable streams.

entries.name: Bacterial culture
entries.definition: Growing bacteria in a laboratory on or in nutrient media in order to isolate, identify or study them.

entries.name: Bacteriology
entries.definition: The branch of microbiology that studies bacteria.

entries.name: Balafon
entries.definition: Playing the balafon, a West African tuned percussion instrument with wooden bars over gourd resonators, struck with mallets.

entries.name: Balloon modelling
entries.definition: Twisting and shaping long, narrow balloons into figures and decorations.

entries.name: Banner advertising
entries.definition: Creating and managing banner ads, the rectangular graphic display advertisements placed on web pages and apps.

entries.name: Banyan VINES
entries.definition: A discontinued network operating system from Banyan Systems, used on enterprise networks in the 1980s and 1990s.

entries.name: Barcode systems
entries.definition: Technology that encodes data as patterns of bars or modules and reads it with scanners to identify products, items or locations.

entries.name: Bariatric surgery
entries.definition: Operations such as gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy that change the stomach or digestive tract to treat severe obesity.

entries.name: Baseline Personnel Security Standard
entries.definition: The UK government's minimum set of pre-employment checks, covering identity, right to work, employment history and unspent criminal convictions.

entries.name: BaseX
entries.definition: A lightweight open-source XML database and XQuery processor.

entries.name: Basic block
entries.definition: A straight-line sequence of program instructions with one entry point and one exit and no branching in between, used in compiler analysis and optimisation.

entries.name: Batman.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript framework, created at Shopify, for building single-page web applications.

entries.name: Battery technology
entries.definition: The science and engineering of electrochemical cells that store and deliver electrical energy, including their chemistries, design, charging and management.

entries.name: Battle management
entries.definition: Directing and coordinating military forces and assets during an operation, using real-time information about the battle.

entries.name: Bed mobility
entries.definition: Helping a patient roll, shift position and move between lying and sitting in bed, and judging how much help they need.

entries.name: Behavior change communication
entries.definition: A public-health approach that uses targeted communication to encourage individuals and communities to adopt healthier behaviours.

entries.name: Behavioural science
entries.definition: The study of human and animal behaviour through observation and experiment, drawing on fields such as psychology, sociology and economics.

entries.name: Benefits realisation management
entries.definition: A discipline of identifying, planning, tracking and delivering the benefits that a project or programme is meant to produce.

entries.name: Bereavement care
entries.definition: Supporting people who are grieving after the death of someone close to them.

entries.name: Berkeley Data Analytics Stack
entries.definition: The open-source big-data software stack developed at UC Berkeley's AMPLab, whose components include Apache Spark and Apache Mesos.

entries.name: Bidirectional-streams Over Synchronous HTTP
entries.definition: An XMPP extension protocol (XEP-0124) that emulates a long-lived two-way connection between client and server using ordinary HTTP request and response pairs.

entries.name: Big O notation
entries.definition: Notation that describes how an algorithm's running time or memory use grows with the size of its input, giving an upper bound.

entries.name: BigFix
entries.definition: An endpoint management platform, now sold by HCL Software, for patching, configuring and securing computers across a network.

entries.name: Bill of materials
entries.definition: A structured list of the raw materials, parts, assemblies and quantities needed to make a product.

entries.name: Binary Ninja
entries.definition: A reverse-engineering platform from Vector 35 for disassembling, decompiling and analysing compiled programs.

entries.name: Binary options
entries.definition: Financial options that pay a fixed amount or nothing, depending on whether an underlying asset meets a set condition at expiry.

entries.name: BIND
entries.definition: Berkeley Internet Name Domain, the widely used open-source DNS server software maintained by the Internet Systems Consortium.

entries.name: Biochemical genetics
entries.definition: The study of how genes control biochemical processes in the body, including inherited metabolic disorders.

entries.name: Bioconductor
entries.definition: An open-source project that distributes R packages for analysing genomic and other biological data.

entries.name: Biological applications of bifurcation theory
entries.definition: The use of bifurcation theory, which studies how the behaviour of a dynamical system changes qualitatively as its parameters vary, to model biological systems.

entries.name: Biomedical informatics
entries.definition: The field that applies information science and computing to the collection, storage and analysis of biological and medical data.

entries.name: Biomolecular engineering
entries.definition: Engineering that designs and modifies biological molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids for use in medicine, industry and research.

entries.name: Biopesticide
entries.definition: Pest-control agents made from natural materials such as microbes, plants and minerals.

entries.name: Biopython
entries.definition: An open-source Python library of tools for computational biology and bioinformatics, such as reading sequence files and working with protein structures.

entries.name: Biosensors
entries.definition: Devices that pair a biological recognition element, such as an enzyme or antibody, with a transducer to detect a specific substance.

entries.name: Bioterrorism preparedness and response
entries.definition: Planning for, detecting and responding to the deliberate release of biological agents that cause disease.
